question: A positive integer \(n\) satisfies the equation \[(n+1)! + (n+2)! = n! \cdot 440.\] What is the sum of the digits of \(n?\)
solution:
The factorials share a factor of \(n!\):
\[
(n+1)!=(n+1)n!,\qquad (n+2)!=(n+2)(n+1)n!.
\]
Dividing the given equation by \(n!\) and simplifying gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
(n+1)+(n+2)(n+1)&=440,\\
n^2+4n+3&=440.
\end{aligned}
\]
Add \(1\) to both sides to complete the square:
\[
n^2+4n+4=441,\qquad (n+2)^2=21^2.
\]
Since \(n\) is positive, \(n+2=21\), so \(n=19\). Its digit sum is \(1+9=\boxed{10}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
